land.text: Hispania: Maximus ruled 'Hispania (the Iberian Peninsula)'; infobox 'in Hispania only'

successors.note: The pages say Gerontius deserted to Constantius, Maximus fled 'amongst the barbarians in Hispania' and Prosper has him pardoned; Hispania itself was in the hands of Vandals, Alans and Suebi (the western-roman-empire dossier). The handover is nominal. [Fix 2026-10-19: Honorius took back north-eastern Hispania and the Gaul Gerontius had held (ledger losses of 411); the rest of Hispania was held by Vandals, Alans and Suebi.] [fx-28: the Gaul in that fix is dropped; no page gives Gerontius or Maximus any Gaul.]

capitals.note: The Gerontius page: after appointing Maximus, 'He moved to Tarraco' (the subject is Gerontius). The Maximus page does not mention Tarraco and names only Barcino (Barcelona, 41.39 N 2.17 E), where 'The mint at Barcino struck coins in his name'.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Territory: Hispania (the Iberian Peninsula)'; infobox 'in Hispania only'. The pages give no extent; Gerontius's allies were Vandals, Alans and Suebi, 'considered the beginning of barbarian invasions in Hispania' (Gerontius page), so the whole peninsula is the maximum. No area. The infobox gives 409-417; the body ends his power c. 411-412, which this keyframe follows. [Fix pass 2026-10-19: the Kingdom of the Suebi page (opened) dates the Vandals', Alans' and Suebi's crossing into Hispania to '28 September or 12 October 409' and their division of the provinces to 411 (Siling Vandals in Baetica, Alans in Lusitania and Carthaginensis, Hasding Vandals and Suebi in Gallaecia), which leaves Tarraconensis, the Tarraco court's province, to Maximus and then to Honorius. The whole peninsula stays drawn as a maximum for 409-410 because no page says when each province was lost to the barbarians and a narrower shape needs loss events against Vandal, Alan and Suebian dossiers that eu-06 owns; the shape overlaps theirs.] Repair fx-28: the Vandal lands are cut out, since the Vandals page has the Vandals in 'Asturia (Northwest)' and 'Hispania Baetica (South)' after the crossing of 13 October 409 and the vandals dossier holds them from 409. [orchestrator 1 Nov 2026, fix-round handoff fx-35: the Alans' Lusitania and Carthaginensis subtracted (Vandals page: the Alans in Lusitania and around Carthago Nova in the 411 division)]

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (reviewer eu-04-x fix): in 411 Gerontius 'successfully besieged and captured Constans in Vienne, executing him' and 'moved on Arelate, where he besieged Constantine' (Gerontius page); the Constantine III page: 'Gerontius caught him at Vienne, probably early in 411, defeated his army and killed Constans' and 'Gerontius's army then marched on Arles and besieged Constantine'. Neither page names the territory; the extent is the one constantine-iii-usurper /ledger/7 and western-roman-empire /ledger/12 already use, and the Gaul passes to Honorius later in 411 (Constantius's arrival), so this shape is a maximum for the year. Repair fx-28: the Gaul part is dropped. The Constantine III page, opened again, names no Gaulish territory that passed to Gerontius or Maximus in 411 (it says only that Gerontius besieged Arles and that the Rhine troops 'abandoned him to support yet another claimant', Jovinus); the land now goes to jovinus-usurper, so the Gaul gain and loss events of this dossier were removed. Repair fx-28: the 411 allotment (Hasdingi in eastern Gallaecia, Silingi in Baetica; vandals ledger 5) is cut out. ledger.note: late spring 409: Gerontius rebels against Constantine III and appoints Maximus emperor. 'In late spring 409, Gerontius rebelled against Constantine'; he 'appointed Maximus as emperor' and 'moved to Tarraco'. The Maximus page dates the installation to late summer 410 ('When Constantine's son Constans arrives with an army, Gerontius mutinies and installs Maximus') and infobox reign 409-417; 409 follows the Gerontius page. The land is the Maximus page's Hispania. Repair fx-28: the Vandal lands (Gallaecia of the Hasdingi, Baetica of the Silingi: Vandals page) are cut out; the Vandals' crossing of the Pyrenees is dated 13 October 409. [orchestrator 1 Nov 2026, fix-round handoff fx-35: without the Alan lands of the 411 allotment (Lusitania, Carthaginensis); Vandals page]

ledger.note: 411: north-eastern Hispania is Honorius's again. Gerontius 'retreated to Hispania with the remainder' and killed himself; Maximus 'loses his main supporter and flees to sanctuary "amongst the barbarians in Hispania"' (Maximus page); Prosper says he was pardoned. No page says that Honorius took Tarraconensis in 411 (page silent): the year and the land are those of western-roman-empire /ledger/13, which this event mirrors (confidence 1). Its /ledger/17 gains more of Tarraconensis from this dossier in 414, after this dossier's end; that one should name nobody or the barbarian holder. [Fix 2026-10-19, reviewer eu-04-x: the dissolve named nobody while western-roman-empire gained the land from this state.]

region.text: the rest of Hispania, where 'the Siling Vandals settled in Hispania Baetica', 'the Alans were allotted the provinces of Lusitania and Hispania Carthaginensis' and 'the Hasding Vandals and the Suevi shared the northwestern province of Gallaecia' in 411 (Kingdom of the Suebi page)

ledger.note: c. 411-412: Gerontius dies and Maximus flees. Gerontius 'defeat[ed] Constantine's forces and kill[ed] Constans at Vienna' in 411, 'but Gerontius later deserts to Constantius, retires to Hispania, and kills himself'; 'Maximus loses his main supporter and flees to sanctuary "amongst the barbarians in Hispania"'; Prosper (412) says he was pardoned when removed from power. The pages give no year for the deposition; 411 is bridged from the Gerontius page's 'In 411' and the end is the researcher's. [Fix 2026-10-19: the dissolve now names western-roman-empire, as the nominal successor (identity.successors) of the part Hispania not taken back in the loss above; the pages put that land in the hands of the Vandals, Alans and Suebi (division of 411, Kingdom of the Suebi page), which are not named here. Thin: the end is still a bridge; the Constantine III page is silent on Maximus's fate, the Gerontius page's reference title gives Gerontius 'd. 411' and the Maximus page's infobox reign runs to 417.]

notes: A rebel state Cliopatria lacks, requested by the eu-04-b report ('Maximus (usurper in Hispania)', 409-411) and by the constantine-iii-usurper dossier. Two pages opened and they disagree: the Gerontius page has the revolt in late spring 409 and Maximus appointed then; the Maximus page has the installation in late summer 410 and an infobox reign 409-417 in Hispania only. The realm is certainly smaller than the whole peninsula (Vandals, Alans and Suebi were in it from 409; the western-roman-empire dossier carries the barbarian shapes); the shape is a maximum. A second Maximus (419-421, captured c. 23 January 422) may be the same man and is not in this dossier. Wikidata id unknown. [Fix pass 2026-10-19: Gerontius's 411 conquests in Gaul (gain from constantine-iii-usurper, loss to western-roman-empire) and the 411 loss of north-eastern Hispania to western-roman-empire added so that constantine-iii-usurper /ledger/7 and western-roman-empire /ledger/12-13 have their counterpart; western-roman-empire /ledger/17 (414 gain from maximus-usurper, conf 1) outlives this dossier and should name nobody or the Suebi/Vandal holders. The pages still do not say whether Gerontius's Gaul was Maximus's; both neighbours treat it as his.]
